patient_note_history:
History 
HPI: A 33-year-old female complains of left knee pain that started two days ago and is causing difficulty in walking. She has swelling and redness in her left knee and a mild fever but no chills. She denies any trauma. She has a history of fatigue and painful wrists and fingers and has experienced one-hour morning stiffness over the past six months. She also recalls multiple oral ulcers that resolved last month. She describes Raynaud’s phenomenon but denies rash, photosensitivity, hair loss, or recent tick bites. She recalls a 10-lb weight loss over the past six months and has no appetite. 
ROS: Negative except as above. 
Allergies: NKDA. 
Medications: Tylenol. 
PMH: Episode of acute left big toe arthritis five years ago; gonorrhea one year ago. 
PSH: Two C-sections, two spontaneous abortions. 
SH: One pack per day for ten years. Usually drinks 2-4 beers/week; on weekends drinks more; last ingestion was four days ago; CAGE 0/4. No illicit drugs. She is sexually active with multiple male partners and inconsistent condom use. 
FH: Her mother has rheumatoid arthritis and lives in a nursing home.

exam_lines.source_text: The patient is in no acute distress but favors the left knee.
VS: WNL except for low-grade fever.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm; S1/S2 within normal limits; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Abdomen: Soft, nondistended, active bowel sounds four times per minute; no hepatosplenomegaly.

Extremities: The patient exhibits erythema, tenderness, pain, and restricted range of motion on flexion and extension of left knee compared to the right knee. There is swelling noted at the left knee. Fingers and hands show stiffness bilaterally. Shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, and ankle joints are within normal limits bilaterally.

gold_target:
Diagnosis #1: Gout 
History Findings: 
- Monoarticular joint pain and tenderness 
- History of swollen toe 
- Occasional alcohol use
Physical Exam Findings: 
- Erythema, tenderness, pain, and restricted range of motion on flexion and extension of left knee compared to the right knee 
- Swelling at the left knee 

Diagnosis #2: Rheumatoid arthritis 
History Findings: 
- Morning joint stiffness 
- Family history of rheumatoid arthritis 
- Systemic symptoms (anorexia, weight loss, fatigue, fever) 
- Multiple joint involvement 
- Duration > 6 weeks 
Physical Exam Findings: 
- Joint tenderness and stiffness 
- Temperature 99.9°F

Diagnosis #3: Systemic lupus erythematosus 
History Findings: 
- Systemic symptoms (anorexia, weight loss, fatigue) 
- History of multiple oral ulcers 
- History of 2 spontaneous abortions 
- Raynaud phenomenon 
Physical Exam Findings: 
- Joint tenderness and stiffness
gold_additional_diagnosis:
• Pseudogout: Another crystal-induced arthritis, pseudogout frequently involves the knees and wrists but is usually seen in patients older than 60 years of age. 

• Gonococcal septic arthritis: This occurs in healthy hosts, most commonly young women (women are much more likely than men to have asymptomatic genitourinary gonococcal infection, which allows the bacteria to mutate and disseminate). The knee is the most frequently involved joint, but the monoarthritis (or tenosynovitis) is usually preceded by a few days of migratory polyarthralgias. Also, this patient does not have the characteristic rash, which consists of small necrotic pustules on the extremities (including the palms and soles). 

• Nongonococcal septic arthritis: This occurs suddenly, usually affects the knee or wrist, and is most commonly caused by S aureus. However, it is a disease of an abnormal host; previous joint damage and IV drug use are key risk factors not present in this case. 

• Osteoarthritis: Onset is insidious, joint stiffness brief, and joint inflammation minimal, all of which are incongruent with this patient's presentation. Also, osteoarthritis spares the wrist and MCP joints and is not associated with constitutional symptoms.

- The examinee made eye contact with the SP.
- The examinee correctly used the patient's name.

Reflective Listening:
- The examinee asked an open-ended question and actively listened to the response.
- The examinee asked the SP to list his/her concerns and listened to the response without interrupting.
- The examinee summarized the SP's concerns, often using the SP's own words.

Information Gathering:
- Examinee dictated data efficiently and accurately.

Sample Closure:

"Ms. Moore, there are a few things that could be causing your knee pain, such as gout, an infection, or rheumatoid arthritis. To determine the cause, I will need to extract fluid from your knee and collect a blood sample.. Sometimes infections from the pelvis can spread to other parts of your body, such as your knee, and for that reason, I would also like to do a pelvic exam. These assessments will probably identify the origin of your discomfort.. You mentioned earlier that you don't always use condoms. I understand that using condoms consistently can be challenging, but they play a vital role in reducing the transmission of STDs.. Do you have any questions for me?" (369 372)
